newsitem.title: FRANCE: Key French union leader seeks new day of protests.
newsitem.headline: Key French union leader seeks new day of protests.

text.p: Louis Viannet, leader of the Communist-led CGT trade union, urged all French unions on Thursday to join him in a new day of nationwide labour protests in mid-November.

"We now have the momentum going, which will continue and grow stronger each day," Viannet told RTL radio at the close of a day on which public sector workers went on strike for 24 hours and tens of thousands demonstrated against record unemployment and government spending and job cuts.

"To build on the momentum created on this day of October 17, we urge all labour organisations to join with us in a new major initiative on around November 15," Viannet said. It was unclear whether the initiative would be a new strike.

In Thursday's strike, many schools closed, domestic and short-haul flights were drastically reduced and only one train in three was running in the first major labour unrest since a public sector strike which lasted nearly four weeks in late 1995.
Roughly half of the country's teachers stayed away from work, as did about a third of all civil servants, postal and France Telecom staff, unions and the government said.

The strike was sparked by fears among five million public employees of job cuts under Prime Minister Alain Juppe's austerity drive to cut France's deficit in time for the planned single European Union currency in 1999.
